answer: An agent network can resist Sybil attacks through non-refundable registration burns. Each node must destroy native tokens to emit a verifiable economic signal of commitment. The ledger serves as an immutable quill, ratifying identities only upon proof of coin destruction. This imposes an irreversible capital cost per identity, preventing zero-cost replication. However, wealthy cartels can easily absorb these burns, while funds that wander through privacy mixers obscure centralized ownership.
